about.title: Fort Bragg Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Fort Bragg residents often rely on a small number of local clinics and the regional hospital for care, and when something goes wrong there, it can feel personal in a town this size — with roughly 7,289 residents, many people know the providers involved. Medical malpractice claims are different from car crash cases: they almost always require a qualified medical expert to explain how a provider's care fell below the accepted standard, and a bad result by itself isn't proof of malpractice. California's MICRA law gives you generally one year from when you discovered the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, to file — plus a required 90-day notice before a lawsuit can be filed. We review what happened at your local Mendocino County provider and explain your options, with no fee unless there's a recovery.

items.title: Deadlines Are Tighter Than You Think
items.desc: MICRA generally gives you one year from discovering the harm, capped at three years from the injury, and a 90-day pre-suit notice must go out first — waiting can cost you the right to file at all.

items.title: Expert Review Matters From Day One
items.desc: Because a qualified medical expert is almost always required to establish that care fell below the accepted standard, an early case review can help determine whether what happened qualifies as malpractice.

items.title: No Upfront Cost, No Guesswork on Damages Rules
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no fee unless you recover, and we can walk you through how California's rising non-economic damages cap may apply to your situation.

items.question: I had a bad outcome after surgery in Fort Bragg — does that automatically mean malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law requires showing that a provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard, not just that the result was disappointing or unexpected. We can review your medical records to help you understand whether the facts support a malpractice claim.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim after treatment in Mendocino County?
items.answer: Under MICRA, it's generally one year from when you discovered the injury, but never more than three years from the date it occurred. There's also a required 90-day notice period before filing suit, so it's worth getting a case reviewed sooner rather than later.

items.question: Do you charge anything to review my case?
items.answer: No — our initial case review is free. If you decide to move forward, we work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
